{"notes": "Visit 2 (left at 3:30). Based only on what I saw and heard. I still don't know who placed which domino, so I'm not crediting or blaming anyone for the build.

Table now: the body is fully connected. The upper arc gap I flagged in visit 1 is closed, but I don't know who closed it. Both arms meet at the crossing (~x21, y10), and the lower tail is connected to ~x25, y13. The whole upper tail loop (~x22-28) is still pale, so it is not connected to the start. The crossing is the problem spot.

Hana: Coordinating again. At 3:00 she said she was bridging the crossing and asked for hands off. At 3:15 she said the bridge wouldn't take, announced she was relaying the lower tail from scratch, and told Omar his upper tail stays. This is clear, calm, protective of others' work and decisive, so leadership and collaboration stay strong. I don't know if the relay was the right call or how it turns out. Check next visit.

Omar: Not seen acting this visit. His upper tail is complete in shape but disconnected. Hana's reassurance suggests it is meant to link up once the crossing works. Ask him privately how he plans to connect it and whether he did the upper arc bridge.

Sofia: First observation. She said she had nudged a stray domino at the crossing, which is honest and open. Then she held hands off to see if Jack's tail catches. That is sensible restraint. I don't know whether her nudge helped or hurt the crossing, since the bridge failed afterward. Her building contribution is still unknown.

Jack: Still nothing seen. Sofia refers to 'Jack's tail', so he may have a stroke in progress. Ask him directly what he placed and whether he's blocked.

Next visit: does the crossing connect, does the upper tail link, and ask each person privately who did what."}
